c.title: Order summary
c.description: Prepare three lines for a pickup desk: full boxes, loose parts, and the order total in cents. Check that the program reads three input numbers.
c.criterion: Input 7 125 3 produces boxes: 2, loose: 1, and total: 875 cents. A missing box capacity produces invalid.

c.title: Unit converter
c.description: Split the work between two functions: one converts minutes to seconds and the other kilometres to metres. The main program selects a function using the code on the first input line.
c.criterion: Code 1 with value 2 gives seconds 120, and code 2 with value 3 gives meters 3000. An unknown code or a value outside 0–30 gives invalid.

c.title: Line filter
c.description: Select short log entries that start with ERR. Process one record at a time to the end of the stream and keep a separate count of rejected records.
c.criterion: ERR fan and ERR are printed unchanged. A record with a leading space is skipped. One overlong record gives rejected 1, and the next valid record is still processed.

c.title: Resizable record list
c.description: Append records to a list that grows as it fills up. Test two controlled allocation failures and determine which work is retained when insertion stops.
c.criterion: For values 20 and 30, modes 0, 1, and 2 give ok 3 4 60, allocation-failed 1 1 10, and allocation-failed 2 2 30 respectively. The last result shows that the first insertion is retained.

c.title: Console inventory
c.description: Build a multi-file program that looks up items, changes quantities, and creates an inventory report from TSV data. Preserve the sources, test inputs, and generated report.
c.criterion: The summary.tsv report has a header and records in their original order with the updated quantity. A duplicate item and an invalid command are rejected, and a repeat report replaces the old data.

steps.title: Define commands and the report format
Implement quantity updates
Test failures and boundaries
Rebuild from a clean directory

onec.title: Service cost calculator
onec.description: Write a BSL function that calculates service cost from duration, an hourly rate, and a discount. Define input bounds and design tests that catch an incorrect formula.
onec.criterion: A 45-minute service at 800 per hour with a 10% discount costs 540, and the caller still holds 45 minutes. Verify zero, a full hour, and rejection of a 101% discount in training 1C.

steps.title: Implement the function and check the caller’s minutes
Work through a rejection and preserve the input
Practise catching an error with a test

onec.title: Service desk
onec.description: Final project. Implement requests, rates as of a given date, request movements, a customer report, and exchange that can be retried by key. Start the query work by checking a join for two customers with the same name.
onec.criterion: The report keeps customers distinct by reference, including a customer with no requests. Repeating a message with the same key does not duplicate the request. Reconcile totals on at least 12 synthetic records and restore the infobase to a fresh directory.

steps.title: Check the join and totals by customer reference
Check exchange retries and key conflicts
Prepare evidence and present the project

onec.title: Synthetic warehouse
onec.description: Final project. Build training stock-in and stock-out workflows by item and warehouse. Apply the register lesson’s balance check to reject issues when stock is insufficient.
onec.criterion: After an allowed issue, the report matches manual reconciliation by warehouse and item. A rejected issue preserves the balance. Reconcile at least 12 synthetic records and verify restoration to a separate infobase.

steps.title: Check receipts, issues, and the balance
Check replacement and reversal of movements
Restore a copy and rerun the checks

onec.title: Training HR documents
onec.description: Final project. Build an event history for fictional employees and departments. Use stable references, a status report, and exchange keyed by event.
onec.criterion: An employee rename preserves the reference and history. Repeating an event does not create duplicates. Reconcile the report against an independent table on at least 12 synthetic records and verify restoration to a new infobase.

steps.title: Check reference stability in the customer example
Apply the retry check to an event
Make a controlled change in a copy

1c-enterprise.title: Two requests from entry to reopening
1c-enterprise.description: Prepare a separate training service desk. Create East and West customer cards, one service, and two requests. Make a controlled edit to practise searching and checking records by number.
1c-enterprise.criterion: Both requests can be found by their actual numbers after reopening. The first retains its new comment and 20 minutes. The second retains its original fields and 55 minutes. A search with no matches leaves the documents unchanged.

steps.title: Prepare a separate training service desk
Save the customer cards
Save and reopen the first request
Add the second request and check both

1c-enterprise.title: Training service desk
1c-enterprise.description: Final project. Build a training infobase to enter and find requests. Link customers, services, durations and statuses, save a report variant, and prepare a backup.
1c-enterprise.criterion: Reconcile identifiers and total minutes for 12 synthetic requests. A filtered report agrees with the independent table. The same records reopen after restoration to a fresh directory, and a controlled edit persists only in the copy.

steps.title: Choose a variant and record the criteria
Build and reconcile the requests
Restore the copy and reconcile the records again
Show an independent change

1c-enterprise.title: Training equipment desk
1c-enterprise.description: Final project. Track requests concerning fictional equipment. Choose service categories, find requests by status, and make one change on a separate copy.
1c-enterprise.criterion: Manually reconcile the identifiers and minutes for the selected status across 12 synthetic requests. An invalid duration is rejected, and a change on the restored copy preserves existing documents and leaves the source intact.

steps.title: Choose the equipment project and plan the checks
Check request cards and durations by number
Test rejection and change only the copy

1c-enterprise.title: Training event desk
1c-enterprise.description: Final project. Track requests from fictional event customers and save a filter and a time-use report. Prepare a backup that can be restored and checked.
1c-enterprise.criterion: For 12 synthetic requests, the report matches the identifiers and minutes in the independent reconciliation. Reopening the saved variant restores its filter, and the recovered infobase shows the original records and total.

steps.title: Choose the event project and set control totals
Apply and reopen a saved report variant
Restore the infobase and reconcile its requests
